references.text: The preceding verse forbids hatred toward your brother in your heart and provides the context for the command to love your neighbor
Cain took revenge on his brother Abel, an early example of violating the prohibition against taking revenge
Practical application of loving your neighbor by helping even your enemy's animals
Encouragement to show kindness to enemies instead of seeking revenge, by giving them food and drink
Jesus quotes this command and expands it to also include love for enemies
Jesus cites this as one of the most important commands
Jesus calls this the second great commandment, equal to the first about loving God
Jesus confirms that loving your neighbor as yourself is the second most important commandment
A lawyer quotes this command, and Jesus tells the parable of the Good Samaritan in response
Paul forbids taking revenge and states that vengeance belongs to the Lord
Paul summarizes the law in the command to love your neighbor as yourself
Paul says that the entire law is fulfilled in this one command about loving your neighbor
James calls this the royal law and confirms its central importance
